:::{#cor-surprisal-discrete-nonnegative}
#### Surprisal of a discrete outcome is nonnegative

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv),
and let $x$ be an outcome with $\P(X=x) > 0$.
Then the [rarity](#def-rarity) of $x$ is at least $1$,
with equality exactly when $\P(X=x) = 1$,
and the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) satisfies

$$\surprisalf{x} \ge 0.$$

:::

::: proof

Since $0 < \P(X=x) \le 1$, the rarity $\rarityf{x} = 1 / \P(X=x)$ is at least $1$,
with equality exactly when $\P(X=x) = 1$.
The logarithm is increasing and $\logf{1} = 0$,
so by @thm-surprisal-log-rarity,
$\surprisalf{x} = \logf{\rarityf{x}} \ge 0$.

:::
